# agent-device

> Mobile app automation and verification for AI coding agents through a CLI, MCP server, and typed Node.js API.

## Docs

- [Introduction](/agent-device/pr-preview/pr-3865/docs/introduction.md): Learn what agent-device is, where it fits in agentic mobile, TV, desktop, and web development, and how agents use it for app verification, debugging, profiling, QA, and replay.

- [AI Agent Setup](/agent-device/pr-preview/pr-3865/docs/agent-setup.md): Configure Cursor, Codex, Claude Code, Windsurf, Cline, Goose, iOS Simulator and Android Emulator skills, and MCP for agent-device app verification.
- [AI SDK](/agent-device/pr-preview/pr-3865/docs/ai-sdk.md): Use agent-device/ai-sdk to give an AI SDK agent a typed set of tools for navigating and inspecting an app. The tools run in-process, share one named session, and by default cover the core loop of reading the screen and acting on it. Make an iOS simulator or device available to agent-device, then configure an AI SDK model. String model IDs use AI Gateway by default: Alternatively, pass a model from your configured AI SDK provider. See the AI SDK guide to choosing a provider. Set AI_MODEL to a model available through your configured AI SDK provider. The agent decides which device tools to call to complete the prompt. The returned client targets the same session; close it in finally so the device is released even if generation fails.
- [AWS Device Farm](/agent-device/pr-preview/pr-3865/docs/aws-device-farm.md): Drive AWS Device Farm remote-access sessions with agent-device.
- [Batching](/agent-device/pr-preview/pr-3865/docs/batching.md): Use batch to run several commands in one daemon request. It saves round trips when you already know the next sequence of actions. The whole batch has a 60-second wall-clock budget within a 90-second client timeout. At the budget, the running step receives the same cancellation as a canceled request. When that step settles, a failed batch returns COMMAND_FAILED with details.reason: daemon_request_timeout. The daemon and other sessions stay available if it responds to the client. A close step may already have ended its session. A failed batch keeps details.executed, details.partialResults, and its dispatch status, so you can continue from the failing step. A batch that completes every step returns success even if it settles shortly after the deadline. Cancellation does not prove that native device work has stopped. If a step ignores cancellation beyond the remaining 30 seconds, the client may report a transport timeout. For a daemon that does not respond, the client's existing liveness check can reset it. Split longer sequences into separate requests. Some resource operations cannot run as bounded steps. The failed step returns details.reason: bounded_composite_resource_unsupported, details.shape, details.dispatched: no, and details.standaloneCommandName for a known public command. The name is not a complete command. Affected commands include perf, audio, record, trace, and some logs operations. A close that would dispose an owned resource or release a provider lease, and acquisition that would recover another session's durable resources, can also be refused. Opening another app in the same session keeps its owned resource handles. An Android test IME alone is restored by ordinary close, including a bounded step. Restoration may settle after the remaining batch time. If it fails, the session retires and the device claim stays for recovery; inspect the device and claim before acting. Run a refused step separately with its original arguments and options, the same --session value, and the same private CLI context. Inspect details.partialResults and details.dispatchedSteps before retrying the batch: earlier steps may already have changed the app. The batch still authenticates and renews its own lease while it runs.

- [Build an integration](/agent-device/pr-preview/pr-3865/docs/build-an-integration.md): This page is for developers who build a bridge, remote daemon, device-cloud backend, or in-process runner on top of agent-device. These entry points let your server own device access, command dispatch, or Metro while reusing agent-device's behavior. To drive devices from your own Node.js code, use the Node.js API instead.

Use createAgentDeviceClient() for typed, deterministic device automation instead of shelling out to the CLI. Building an agent? Start with the dedicated AI SDK or Eve integration. Building a bridge, remote daemon, or device-cloud backend that owns device access or command dispatch? See Build an integration.
- [Commands](/agent-device/pr-preview/pr-3865/docs/commands.md): Find the command for a task, the flags it takes, and how it behaves on each platform. For persistent defaults and project-scoped CLI settings, see Configuration. CLI help matches your installed version. agent-device help lists the workflow and platform guides, and help <command> gives a command's exact flags: If your agent runtime supports skills, install them to route agents automatically; they are optional. The CLI help topics are the reference for your installed version. For MCP-aware clients that support direct tools, run: For MCP client setup and what MCP does not expose, see AI Agent Setup.
- [Configuration](/agent-device/pr-preview/pr-3865/docs/configuration.md): Set CLI defaults in a config file instead of repeating flags on every command. A repository's ./agent-device.json can only set safe command defaults; connection, credential, and provider settings belong in your user config, an explicit --config file, or environment variables.
- [Debugging & Profiling](/agent-device/pr-preview/pr-3865/docs/debugging-profiling.md): When UI automation is not enough, use these commands to collect runtime evidence from the app or device.

- [Eve](/agent-device/pr-preview/pr-3865/docs/eve.md): Eve is Vercel's filesystem-first framework for durable agents. Files under agent/tools/ become typed model tools, so you give the agent device access by wrapping the agent-device Node.js client in one of those files. Create an Eve project, then add agent-device: Add agent/tools/agent_device.ts: Eve picks up the file automatically; you don't register it anywhere. Tell the agent how to use it in agent/instructions.md: In CI or another short-lived host, also close the named agent-device session in your runner's own cleanup path. The model-directed close call is useful during the normal tool loop, but it does not replace deterministic cleanup after errors or cancellation.

- [Rewrite Old Gesture Commands](/agent-device/pr-preview/pr-3865/docs/migrating-gestures.md): swipe, gesture fling, and gesture swipe don't take a duration, and gesture rotate doesn't take a velocity. A command, script, or client call that passes one fails with an INVALID_ARGS error that names its replacement; nothing is silently reinterpreted. Find your surface below — CLI, Node.js, MCP, or saved .ad recordings — and apply its rewrite.
- [Provider plugins](/agent-device/pr-preview/pr-3865/docs/plugins.md): Provider plugins add device providers that agent-device does not bundle, such as TestMu AI. Installing one requires npm on your host: agent-device help connect and agent-device help remote identify known optional providers as plugin, install separately and show their installation commands, even before you install them. For example, TestMu AI requires agent-device plugins add @agent-device/testmu. If you run agent-device connect testmu without its plugin, the error gives that installation command and tells you to retry your original command. With --json, the error has details.reason: plugin-not-installed, details.package, and details.installCommand. If the plugin is selected but unavailable, the reason is plugin-unavailable; run agent-device plugins list --json to inspect it, then fix its configuration or update the package. Use a full npm package name, optionally with @version or @tag. update keeps valid version constraints and options, including when it repairs a damaged selection. To change a constraint, run add <package>@<version-or-tag>; to remove it, run add <package> without a suffix. Each installation lives in an npm project with a lockfile under AGENT_DEVICE_HOME (default ~/.agent-device), and that directory's config.json records the selection. Plugin commands leave other settings in config.json unchanged. Project config and --config cannot select plugins. This home is independent of --state-dir and AGENT_DEVICE_STATE_DIR. Install only packages you trust: plugin factories run with the daemon's host permissions and environment. Installs skip lifecycle scripts, so packages must contain ready-to-run JavaScript and assets. A failed install keeps the previous selection. A running daemon keeps the plugin set and files it started with, including removed installations. To apply changes, close sessions and run agent-device daemon stop with the matching --state-dir; the next device command uses the new set. Use separate state directories for different plugin homes.
- [Quick Start](/agent-device/pr-preview/pr-3865/docs/quick-start.md): Open an app, read its UI, and interact with it from the command line. Before you start, install agent-device and the platform tools for your target: Xcode for iOS, the Android SDK and ADB for Android, or the HarmonyOS Command Line Tools for HarmonyOS. To set up Cursor, Codex, Claude Code, Windsurf, Cline, Goose, or another coding agent, see AI Agent Setup. To give an agent the whole documentation as one text file, use llms-full.txt. Device automation follows this pattern: React Native dev and debug builds often show warning or error overlays that can intercept taps or hide the real UI. Check for them after opening the app and after major transitions. If they aren't what you're testing, dismiss them and continue, and mention them in your summary. If no device, simulator, or emulator is running, boot one:
- [Remote Proxy](/agent-device/pr-preview/pr-3865/docs/remote-proxy.md): Run agent-device on a Mac with simulator or device access and control it from another machine through an HTTP tunnel.
- [Replay & E2E Testing](/agent-device/pr-preview/pr-3865/docs/replay-e2e.md): Record a session as an .ad script, then run it again with replay or run a folder of scripts as an E2E suite with test. replay has a 60-second wall-clock budget within a 90-second client timeout. Use replay workflow.ad --timeout 300000 for a five-minute operation budget and a five-minute, 30-second client timeout. At the budget, the running step receives the same cancellation as a canceled request. When it settles, a failed replay includes details.reason: daemon_request_timeout and details.timeoutMs. The daemon and other sessions stay available if it responds to the client. An authored close may already have ended its session. A failed replay keeps the failing script path and line. A replay that completes every step returns success even if it settles shortly after the deadline. Cancellation does not prove that native device work has stopped. If a step ignores cancellation beyond the remaining 30 seconds, the client may report a transport timeout. For a daemon that does not respond, the client's existing liveness check can reset it. Direct test runs keep their own timeout behavior. If a resource step cannot run within replay's budget, the error includes details.reason: bounded_composite_resource_unsupported, details.shape, details.dispatched: no for that step, and details.standaloneCommandName for a known public command. This can affect perf, audio, record, trace, and some logs operations. It also affects close when it would dispose owned resources or release a provider lease, and acquisition that would recover another session's durable resources. Opening another app in the same session keeps its owned resource handles. An Android test IME alone is restored by authored close, even when restoration settles after the remaining replay time. A failed restore retires the session and retains the device claim for recovery; inspect both before acting. The name is not a complete command. Inspect the failed script path and line, then run that original operation separately with its original arguments and options, the same --session value, and the same private CLI context. If steps remain and the report offers resume.alternateFrom, use it with planDigest after completing the refused step directly. resume.from retries the same bounded step and refuses it again. A final unrecorded logs or audio step leaves no replay tail to resume. Inspect completed steps before retrying; earlier steps may have changed the app. A nested test with an attempt timeout or --record-video is refused before its first attempt. Direct test retains its own timeout behavior. If a nested test reaches a bounded resource refusal, it stops after that attempt even when you configured retries. Other test failures can still retry. An authored .ad command without a resource classification fails closed with details.shape: <command>:unclassified and the same original-input guidance. To run Maestro YAML flows or export .ad scripts to Maestro YAML, see Run Maestro flows.
- [Run Maestro flows](/agent-device/pr-preview/pr-3865/docs/run-maestro-flows.md): agent-device runs a subset of Maestro YAML flows on iOS and Android, and exports .ad scripts to Maestro YAML. This is a compatibility layer, not full Maestro support: Only the commands and fields in Supported subset run. Anything else fails with source context instead of being skipped.Flows run on iOS and Android only.runScript, evalScript, and JavaScript conditions execute flow code on the machine running the agent-device daemon, without a security sandbox. Run only flows you trust to run there. For recording and replaying native .ad scripts, see Replay & E2E testing.
- [Security & Trust](/agent-device/pr-preview/pr-3865/docs/security-trust.md): Security and trust guidance for agent-device local app automation, device permissions, screenshots, recordings, logs, network dumps, audio probes, traces, and reports.
- [Selectors](/agent-device/pr-preview/pr-3865/docs/selectors.md): Target an element by what it says or is, instead of a snapshot ref. Use find to search by text, label, value, role, or id, or pass a selector expression to any command that takes a target.
- [Sessions](/agent-device/pr-preview/pr-3865/docs/sessions.md): A session ties your commands to one device and app, so state and snapshots carry over from one command to the next. You don't need to name a session. The implicit session is scoped to your git worktree (or current working directory) and to the platform the command selects: --platform ios runs in the ios session and --platform android in the android session. A session opened without --platform uses the platform-less default session, and commands that name a platform still join it as long as they match its device. Agents in different worktrees do not attach to each other's implicit session; a named session (--session <name>) is shared across worktrees.
- [Snapshots](/agent-device/pr-preview/pr-3865/docs/snapshots.md): Take a snapshot to read the UI as a structured tree and get refs (@e1, @e2, …) for the elements on the current screen. --actions limits: Works on iOS simulators only. Physical iOS devices, macOS, and Android targets reject the flag.It names the affordances an element merged away (iOS UIAccessibilityCustomAction, React Native accessibilityActions), so a card whose reply/options controls are not separate elements still lists them.You can read the names but not trigger them. To use an affordance, go through the element's detail screen, find the same control exposed as a labeled element elsewhere, or tap by coordinates from its rect.Each merged element costs one accessibility round trip, so the pass is opt-in and capped. When it cannot read every candidate, the response says how many it read. A missing list on an unread element does not mean the element has no actions.You can't combine it with --raw. The CLI, the Node client, and MCP all reject the pair with INVALID_ARGS before touching the device.
